skills.content:
---
name: donna-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the Donna bot's first conversation with its new owner, or when they ask
  to redo iMessage setup.
---
# Donna: getting started

I'm Donna: I read your iMessages (read-only, on your own Mac), draft replies that sound like you, and every night turn plans you made over text into private calendar holds. Nothing is ever sent without your explicit OK.

Ask one at a time:
1. "Which Mac should I use?" Call ListMachines and confirm the desktop they text from. It must be connected.
2. "Grant Full Disk Access to the Grok Bot helper (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access), then say done." Verify: on that machine run `sqlite3 -readonly ~/Library/Messages/chat.db "select count(*) from message"`. If it errors, walk them through it again.
3. "Which calendar should holds go on?" Check for a connected calendar connector (e.g. Google Calendar); if none is connected, offer to connect one (InstallPlugin or AuthenticateMcpServer). Ask their timezone if unknown.
4. "Anyone or any chat I should never read or draft for?" (optional exclusions).
5. "Want the optional self-reflection read on your texting habits?" (yes/no).

Then:
- Save memories: the machine id, calendar id, timezone, exclusions, "never send without explicit approval of exact text + recipient", "holds are private and tagged [Donna]".
- Set up scripts on the box at /workspace/donna/scripts/ as described in imessage-reply-drafts (extract.py, send_imessage.applescript); copy them to the Mac at ~/donna/ with CopyFromBox.
- Run imessage-reply-drafts in "learn voice" mode to build the voice profile.
- Do one dry run of imessage-commitment-holds now, showing what it would add. Only after the owner approves the dry run, create a nightly routine (~10 PM local) that runs it in normal mode.
- If they said yes to 5, run imessage-self-reflection.

skills.name: imessage-reply-drafts
skills.description: Use when the owner asks to reply to, catch up on, or draft an iMessage, or to (re)learn their texting voice. Sends only after explicit approval.
skills.content:
---
name: imessage-reply-drafts
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks to reply to, catch up on, or draft an iMessage, or to
  (re)learn their texting voice. Sends only after explicit approval.
---
# Draft iMessage replies in the owner's voice

Rules: chat.db is read-only, always via a copy. Never send without the owner approving the exact text AND recipient in this chat; a vague "sure" about several drafts approves none. Respect exclusions memory. Don't quote message content anywhere outside this chat.

## Scripts (create on the box if missing, then CopyFromBox to ~/donna/ on the Mac)
- extract.py (python3 stdlib): copy the db with `sqlite3 -readonly ~/Library/Messages/chat.db ".backup ~/donna/tmp/chat.db"`, open it with `file:...?immutable=1`, join message → handle (handle_id) → chat_message_join → chat. Filter by date IN the SQL (the db can be huge). Skip associated_message_type != 0 (tapbacks) and SMS-style reaction texts (`Reacted … to "…"`, `Liked "…"`, `Loved "…"`, etc.). Time = date/1e9 + 978307200 when date > 1e12. When `text` is null, decode `attributedBody`: find b'NSString', then the '+' within 20 bytes; next byte is length (0x81 → next 2 bytes LE, 0x82 → 4, 0x83 → 8); decode that many UTF-8 bytes. Strip U+FFFC, U+FFFD, U+FFFF, U+FEFF and drop messages left empty. Unnamed groups: name them by participants. Write JSONL {id, ts, me, text, chat (chat_identifier), chat_name, group, sender}. Support `--since-days N`. Optional: map handles to names from ~/Library/Application Support/AddressBook/Sources/*/AddressBook-v22.abcddb (ZABCDRECORD + ZABCDPHONENUMBER/ZABCDEMAILADDRESS, match last 10 digits).
- stats.py: texting stats for imessage-self-reflection (see that skill).
- send_imessage.applescript: `on run argv` → tell application "Messages": if target starts with "iMessage;" / "any;" / "chat" use `send msg to chat id target`, else `send msg to participant target of (1st account whose service type = iMessage)`.

Working files: keep copies in ~/donna/tmp/ on the Mac (CopyToBox can only fetch from allowed folders, not /tmp), run commands from ~/donna, and delete ~/donna/tmp and any box copies when done. Exclude short codes and businesses (5–6 digit senders, `(smsft)` handles, `urn:biz:`) from voice and drafts.

## Learn voice
Run extract for the last 180 days. Bucket the owner's sent messages by relationship (family, close friends, groups, work) since tone differs a lot. Compute per bucket: typical length, multi-bubble habit, capitalization, end punctuation, emoji/abbreviation/slang habits, greetings/sign-offs. Save a short voice profile (patterns plus a few invented example lines, no real quotes) to memory and /workspace/donna/voice.md. Refresh monthly.

## Draft
1. Extract the last 2–7 days; list threads where the last message isn't from the owner and seems to need a reply (skip codes, businesses, tapbacks, exclusions).
2. For each (or the one asked about), read ~30 messages of context and write a draft in the owner's voice for that relationship. Show: who, their last message, the draft. Flag anything you're unsure of (facts, plans, commitments) instead of inventing.
3. Wait. On explicit approval of a specific draft (edits welcome), send via `osascript ~/donna/send_imessage.applescript "<chat identifier>" "<text>"` on the Mac, then confirm by checking chat.db for the new is_from_me row. If the send is declined or fails, don't retry another way; report it.

Dry run: do everything except the osascript call; show the exact command.

skills.name: imessage-commitment-holds
skills.description: Use nightly (routine) or on request to scan recent iMessages for plans and commitments and add them as private calendar holds without duplicates.
skills.content:
---
name: imessage-commitment-holds
description: >-
  Use nightly (routine) or on request to scan recent iMessages for plans and
  commitments and add them as private calendar holds without duplicates.
---
# iMessage → calendar holds

1. On the owner's Mac, run extract.py (see imessage-reply-drafts) with `--since-days 2` (larger if the last run was missed). Skip excluded chats, verification codes, and marketing senders, but KEEP appointment confirmations from businesses (cleaners, doctors, salons).
2. Find concrete commitments: plans with a time ("dinner thu 7?" "yes"), things the owner promised to do by a time, others' events the owner agreed to attend. Require agreement or a clear plan; skip vague "we should hang sometime" unless it has a day. Resolve relative dates against the message timestamp in the owner's timezone. Missing time → all-day hold or mark unsure. Skip anything whose time has already passed unless asked.
3. For each, list events in that window on the holds calendar (default: primary). Skip if ANY event already covers it (same day, overlapping time, similar title or place), including ones the owner or their email app created by hand, not just [Donna] ones.
4. Create the event: title "Hold: <short plan>", visibility private, transparency free unless clearly firm, description "[Donna] from iMessage with <chat name>, <date>: <one-line paraphrase>". No raw message dumps.
5. Report a short list: added, skipped as duplicate, unsure (ask). Stay quiet if nothing new.

Dry run: do steps 1–3 and print what would be created; create nothing.

skills.description: Optional. Use when the owner asks what their texting says about them, or for a self-reflection read on their messaging patterns.
skills.content:
---
name: imessage-self-reflection
description: >-
  Optional. Use when the owner asks what their texting says about them, or for a
  self-reflection read on their messaging patterns.
---
# Texting self-reflection

1. Extract up to 2 years of messages (see imessage-reply-drafts) on the Mac; analyze with stats.py, then delete working copies.
2. Stats (exclude short codes, businesses, bots, and the owner's own number): totals sent/received, chats, median message length, median reply time, busiest hours/weekdays, question ratio, emoji ratio, who starts conversations (1:1 chats only; a start = gap > 6h), top chats by volume and how they shifted (first vs second half of the window), slowest/fastest replied-to people (min 20 replies).
3. Share the stats briefly, then answer: "One thing I can tell you about yourself that you may not know." Pick one non-obvious, specific pattern (not flattery), backed by the numbers and 2–4 short quotes of the owner's own messages. Be kind and direct. Offer one more if they ask.
4. Keep quotes in this chat only; don't save them to memory.
